notes.chunk_at_written: The scientist Eastman bought a company to hire went on to mentor Edwin Land, who built Polaroid into the company Eastman might have built with a second chance: instant chemistry inside a consumer camera, defended by patents, run by a founder who was himself the product. Land Kodak for copying him and won 925 million dollars, the largest patent judgment American courts had ever produced and the largest for the next quarter century. Land was then forced out of Polaroid after the Polavision failure and resigned the chairmanship in 1982. Polaroid filed for bankruptcy in October 2001, eleven years ahead of Kodak, killed by digital and by the debt it had taken on to fight off a hostile takeover.
notes.stood_on: Land Kodak for copying him and won 925 million dollars, the largest patent judgment American courts had ever produced and the largest for the next quarter century.
notes.answered_by: For more than a decade Kodak manufactured the negative material inside every Polaroid picture, and it spent years demanding a license to enter instant photography as the price of continuing to supply it.
